card.name: Linking words in overdose and ingestion text
card.fires_on: Small linking words or punctuation (and, of, by, from, comma, after) in overdose or accidental-ingestion passages, just before a stomach or gut term like gastric lavage or absorption. Also after meal-timing phrases.

modes.label: Overdose management
modes.description: Small word or comma in an overdosage section just before measures such as emptying the stomach or limiting absorption.
modes.example: Immediately after ingestion of an overdose, further absorption of the drug may be minimized<< by>> inducing vomiting or by gastric lavage,

modes.label: Ingestion and meals
modes.description: Linking word after eating or swallowing something, or after a meal-timing phrase.
modes.example: Animals can climb inside and suffocate, or eat them<< and>> choke.

modes.label: Accidental ingestion advice
modes.description: Comma after an accidental ingestion clause, before the instruction to call poison control.
modes.example: If accidental ingestion occurs<<,>> call your Poison Control Center.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about digestion and the stomach.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words where the text is about swallowing something or an overdose, and the next idea is about the stomach or digestion.
